<details>
<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

Adds an exported helper GetLatestSupportedOCPVersion(ctx, client) in support/supportedversion/version.go. The function calls the existing GetSupportedOCPVersions (using namespace "hypershift"), ensures the returned SupportedVersions.Versions slice is non-empty, and parses the first advertised version by appending ".0" into a semver.Version. It returns errors when the ConfigMap/versions are missing or when semver parsing fails. No changes were made to retrieveSupportedOCPVersion. Tests: a new unit test for GetLatestSupportedOCPVersion and an e2e test updated to conditionally remove a NodePool condition based on the retrieved version.

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as Test / Caller
    participant K8sClient as Kubernetes API (client)
    participant ConfigMap as ConfigMap "supported-versions" (hypershift)
    participant JSON as JSON Parser
    participant Semver as Semver Parser

    Caller->>K8sClient: Call GetSupportedOCPVersions(namespace="hypershift")
    K8sClient-->>Caller: ConfigMap (or not found)
    alt ConfigMap not found
        Caller-->>Caller: return error "supported versions not found"
    else ConfigMap found
        Caller->>JSON: unmarshal ConfigMap.Data["supported-versions"] -> SupportedVersions
        JSON-->>Caller: SupportedVersions (Versions list)
        Caller->>Caller: if Versions empty -> return error "no supported versions"
        Caller->>Semver: parse Versions[0] + ".0"
        Semver-->>Caller: semver.Version or parse error
        alt parse success
            Caller-->>Caller: return semver.Version
        else parse failure
            Caller-->>Caller: return parse error
        end
    end
```

</details>

>## What this PR does / why we need it:
>
>The NodePoolSupportedVersionSkewConditionType condition is only set starting in OCP 4.21 (PR #5931). The backup/restore e2e test validates all expected NodePool conditions, causing failures on older clusters.
>
>Add GetLatestSupportedOCPVersion helper to supportedversion package and use it in the backup/restore test to skip the SupportedVersionSkew condition when the operator's latest supported version is < 4.21.
>
>This is important in jobs that use MCE and the Hypershift operator in MCE is not the latest one. Hence it doesn't set the condition on the NodePool and it's missing there.
>
>## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
>Fixes 
>Related [slack thread](https://redhat-internal.slack.com/archives/G01QS0P2F6W/p1774354039382309?thread_ts=1773823435.605839&cid=G01QS0P2F6W)
>

>- [x] Subject and description added to both, commit and PR.
>- [x] Relevant issues have been referenced.
>- [ ] This change includes docs. 
>- [ ] This change includes unit tests.
>
>

>> [!NOTE]
>> **Low Risk**
>> Low risk: changes are limited to adding a small helper for reading the operator’s advertised supported versions and using it to adjust an e2e test expectation; no production reconciliation or API behavior is modified.
>> 
>> **Overview**
>> Backup/restore e2e pre-checks now **conditionally drop** the `NodePoolSupportedVersionSkewConditionType` from expected NodePool conditions when the HyperShift operator advertises a latest supported OCP version < `4.21`, avoiding failures on older operator installs.
>> 
>> This introduces `supportedversion.GetLatestSupportedOCPVersion`, which reads the `supported-versions` ConfigMap in the `hypershift` namespace and returns the newest advertised version, with unit tests covering missing/empty/malformed ConfigMap scenarios.
